Subject: Structured output reliability — follow-up & next steps

Hi Alex / Priya,

Thanks again for taking the demo today — appreciate the thoughtful questions on structured output and reliability. Quick recap and proposed next steps: 

1) What we heard
- You need deterministic JSON responses for downstream ingestion (order/fields matter)
- Validation and automatic retry patterns are critical given occasional model hallucination/format drift
- Runtime constraints: 500ms median latency target, some calls will be in high-throughput batch mode for nightly rerank jobs

2) Redwood suggestions (high-level)
- Constrained decoding + JSON schema enforcement at generation time (we demonstrated the schema enforcement prototype)
- Post-generation validation with structured retry pattern: re-prompt + more constrained decode on failure, plus a lightweight sanitizer for known edge-cases
- Hybrid routing: low-latency single-token decoding for interactive calls, and batched high-throughput variants for nightly rerank/embedding flows

3) Action items / next steps
- I will share an architecture stub (attached) showing SDK auth, routing, and where constrained decoding/validation fits. /Marissa
- Aditya to review the proposed retry heuristic and recommended prompt templates (cc'ing him)
- Alex / Priya — confirm which endpoints are interactive vs batch, and share a sample JSON schema you want enforced (we can iterate on this together)

Attachments: redwood-arch-diagram.png (architecture stub), structured-output-playbook.pdf (patterns + suggested prompts)

If that aligns I can coordinate a short technical call next week (30m) with our infra engineer Logan and Aditya.

Thanks,

--
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>

Subject: Re: Structured output reliability — follow-up & next steps

Marissa,

Thanks for the clear recap — that looks good. Couple of clarifying questions before we sync: 

- SDK / auth: we use OAuth2 with short-lived tokens and a central AuthZ proxy. Do you support token introspection and automatic credential rotation in the SDK? What's the recommended pattern for private deployments?
- Schema enforcement: if the model fails to adhere after 3 retries, can Redwood fall back to a deterministic parser (e.g., a template-based extractor) and surface the failure to our logs?
- Embeddings / rerank: for nightly reranks we will likely send batched embedding requests and then run a reranker model against top-K. Need guidance on cost controls (batch size/quantization) and how to route those to dedicated capacity.

We can confirm endpoints — interactive: /chat/generate, batch: /embeddings/batch and /rerank. I'll also attach a sample schema for the primary response (will forward separately).

Can you loop in your infra engineer for a 30m technical sync next Wed (Mar 4) morning PT?

Best,
Alex

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-03T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: FW: Structured output reliability — follow-up & next steps

Looping in Logan for the architecture + routing questions. Initial notes: 

- SDK: our JS/Go SDK supports OAuth2 bearer tokens and integrates with customer KMS for Private deployments. We have a token refresh hook and a credential rotation guide in the playbook.
- Routing: recommend policy-based routing — interactive requests -> low-latency pool (smaller batch sizes, pinned weights), batch reranks -> dedicated capacity with autoscale and quantized models for cost savings. We'll annotate the diagram (redwood-arch-diagram.png) with suggested routing rules.
- Retry/validation pattern (draft):
  1) Generate with constrained decoding (schema tokens locked where possible)
  2) Validate JSON against schema client-side (fast lib)
  3) On failure: re-prompt with stricter constraints, increase temperature control -> re-generate up to 2 retries
  4) If still invalid: fallback to deterministic parser and return a flagged response (error_code + raw_output) so app can decide (we log and surface in Console)

I'll prepare a short slot for Wed morning PT — Logan, which times work? I can do 8:30–10:00am PT.

- Aditya

Alex / Priya — thanks for the quick turnaround.

Short answers to your questions: 

- SDK / auth: yes — our hosted SDKs support OAuth2 with automatic refresh hooks. For Private deployments we support integration with your IdP and KMS-based key rotation. I'll attach the relevant SDK auth snippet in the Drive folder (see related links).
- Failed schema enforcement: after 2 automated retries we fall back to the deterministic extractor and return a structured response with an error flag and the raw model output. We surface these incidents in Console and can wire up a webhook to push these events to your SRE/Observability tool.
- Embeddings / rerank routing & cost controls: recommend using dedicated capacity for large nightly jobs. Suggested knobs: max batch size 256, quantized model profile for embeddings, and a per-job token budget. We'll include concrete recommendations in the playbook.

Proposed tech sync: Wed Mar 4, 9:30am PT — 30m (Logan + Aditya + Marissa). If that works I'll send a calendar invite and a short agenda: 1) auth/SDK integration 2) routing & capacity 3) concrete retry + validation flow + sample schema enforcement.

Next steps for you two (Alex / Priya): please confirm 1) the sample JSON schema (attach or paste) and 2) whether you want the webhook for failed validations to go to your Observability team (if so, share the endpoint).

Thanks again — looking forward to the sync.
